title: Dashboard transactional timeline: skeleton & progressive-loading visual review and handoff
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Scope: define and finalize the visual system for the dashboard 'transactional timeline' component's loading states across density modes and rollouts. This ticket captures design review cycles, redlines for dev handoff, QA checks, and stakeholder feedback synthesis. The timeline is used in Cost Insights and Rollouts pages where users view a sequence of events (deploy, scale, fallback). We need a skeleton state that communicates structure quickly without implying final content or causing layout shift when real data loads.

Goals:
- Create a low-distraction skeleton that matches final typography rhythm and spacing so content jump is minimal.
- Ensure skeleton variants for dense / default density and mobile breakpoints.
- Provide motion guidelines (reduced motion friendly).
- Deliver annotated redlines, Figma components, and a small interactive prototype for engineering and QA.

Non-goals: proposing new row metadata or altering timeline data model (ENG to own API mapping).
acceptance_criteria: Figma component library contains 'timeline-skeleton' tokenized for spacing and color
Redlines document with pixel measurements and margin collapse rules uploaded to Confluence
Prototype demonstrates skeleton to content transition with and without motion preference
Engineering receives a clear QA checklist and 2 example datasets to validate layout stability
Accessibility check: contrast and reduced-motion behavior validated by design during review
decisions: Use subtle gradient shimmer only for promotional/hint states; default skeleton uses solid low-contrast blocks to reduce perceived motion and avoid eye fatigue.
Reserve shimmer animation behind a feature flag for canary rollout and performance testing.
Adopt consistent 8px vertical rhythm for timeline rows; compact density multiplies vertical gaps by 0.7.
Do not render timestamp placeholders in skeleton to avoid perceived content accuracy—use dots instead to indicate temporal slots.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Shimmer improves perceived progress but introduces continuous animation that may distract power users and increase GPU work on low-end devices.
Avoiding timestamps in skeleton reduces clarity on row mapping; engineers need to ensure minimal layout shift when timestamps load.
Introducing multiple skeleton variants increases implementation surface for engineering and QA time.
review_feedback: Ravi Patel (PM): prefer clearer affordance for rows that will include expandable details; suggested a thin divider treatment in dense mode.
Sophie Morales (Eng): raised performance concerns for shimmer across large lists; requested a non-animated fallback and a batch-rendering plan (virtualization).
Janelle Ortiz (Accessibility): requested contrast checks on skeleton color tokens and a documented reduced-motion fallback; suggested swapping shimmer for a pulse on reduced-motion false only.
Design leadership (Ava Brooks): asked to consolidate skeleton token names to match console theme tokens to avoid token proliferation.
redlines_and_handoff: Exported @1x and @2x PNGs for pixel review added to Drive folder
Component naming conventions: timeline-skeleton-row, timeline-skeleton-dot, timeline-skeleton-divider
Edge cases: single-row timeline, empty-state timeline, timeline with avatars (reserve 40px avatar gap)
Dev handshake call scheduled: 2026-03-14 11:00 PT (calendar invite sent)
